supporting_observations.claim: The alerted pattern is present: proxy CONNECT requests to update.medledger.co occur from 13:36:39 through 14:06:26 at roughly five-minute intervals, with one request returning status 504.

The connections are associated in endpoint telemetry with medledgerupd.exe running as tom.weber from C:\Users\tom.weber\AppData\Local\MediLedger; the process connects to the explicit proxy at 10.51.20.30:8080.

The supplied inventory describes MediLedger checks to update.medledger.com and an updater under Program Files, whereas these logs show update.medledger.co and an updater under the user's AppData directory. This discrepancy needs verification; it does not by itself establish maliciousness.

The proxy records report a Firefox user agent for the MediLedger destination, while endpoint network events attribute the proxy connections to medledgerupd.exe; the available records do not explain this difference.
The updater process terminated shortly after its last logged connection, at 14:06:35 UTC.

known_telemetry_limitations: Endpoint events show connections to the explicit proxy, not direct connections from WS-TWEBER-01 to the external destination; the proxy CONNECT records identify the requested hostname.
The supplied records do not expose the tunneled HTTPS content, certificate details, destination IP, or full request and response data.
The records do not provide the updater's hash, signature status, installation source, or vendor validation.
The proxy user-agent field does not establish which process generated that header.
claims_not_established: Whether update.medledger.co is controlled by MediLedger or is an unauthorized lookalike.
Whether the AppData executable is a legitimate MediLedger build, a legitimate relocated installation, or an unauthorized binary.
Whether the periodic requests carried only update-check traffic or other content.
Whether the Firefox user-agent value reflects normal application behavior, configuration, or spoofing.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the executable's hash, signature and certificate details, file metadata, and installation or download provenance; verify these with the MediLedger vendor or internal software records.
Review proxy and DNS records for destination resolution, certificate metadata, complete CONNECT details, and any related requests or security detections.
Confirm with the application owner and vendor whether update.medledger.co and an AppData installation path are expected for this workstation.
Investigate why the proxy reports a Firefox user agent for connections attributed by endpoint telemetry to medledgerupd.exe.
